candidate.title: git --attr-source <word> makes the shell analyser read a fake read-only subcommand while git runs any command, with -c config keys
candidate.description: The shell analyser walks git's global options with a hard-coded list of value-taking options. It treats every other dash-word as a flag without a value. Git's --attr-source takes the next word as its value. In `git --attr-source status <rest>` the analyser sees the subcommand `status`, which is on the read-only list, and approves the command. Git treats `status` as the tree-ish and runs `<rest>` instead, including `-c` global config keys that the analyser refuses elsewhere. An agent under the hunt, QA or autopilot profile can therefore run git commit, config, fetch, clone, reset or clean on the host, and can run arbitrary shell commands with `-c alias.x='!cmd' x`. The hunt forbids writes outside reviews/<ID>/ and .ultrapowers/, egress and project code on the host, and this bypasses all three.
candidate.root_cause: GIT_GLOBAL_WITH_ARG omits --attr-source, and the global-option loop skips any other dash-word without consuming a value. The analyser's idea of the subcommand therefore differs from git's.
candidate.intended_behavior: Only a git subcommand on the profile's list may run, and `-c`, `--config-env` and `--exec-path` must never reach git. The subcommand the analyser judges must be the subcommand git runs.

trace.description: A Bash tool call from the agent is handed to the quote-aware analyser (qa-shell-writes.mjs analyze) under the hunt, qa or autopilot profile.
The list of git global options that take a value has -C, -c, --git-dir, --work-tree, --namespace and --exec-path. It lacks --attr-source.
`if (v.startsWith('-')) { k++; continue; }` skips --attr-source as a no-value flag, so the next word, `status`, becomes rest[k] and the subcommand.
The refusal runs only over rest[0..k). A `-c` after the fake subcommand is outside that range and is not examined.
`status` is in GIT_READ_ONLY, so the command returns with no denial. Git runs the real subcommand and the -c config keys that follow.

evidence.description: sub = rest[k].v, with k set by the loop that does not know --attr-source.
The skip-as-flag rule is the only handling of unknown dash options before the subcommand.

The only text-level git rules are for push, merge, rebase, cherry-pick and discard forms. None checks -c or an alias, so no later layer catches an alias-based command. I read this at the source and did not test each text rule.

conditions.description: The host git must accept `--attr-source <tree-ish>` with a space (git 2.56.0.windows.2 does). Older git without --attr-source (before 2.40) fails with an error and does not run the command.
The caller is the agent under an active hunt, QA or autopilot guardrail, steered by content it reads.

execution.attacker_perspective: The agent, or content steering it, sends a Bash call under an active guardrail profile.
instructions: In a sandbox, import hooks/lib/qa-shell-writes.mjs and call analyze(command, {cwd, root, ticket, profile, ignoreCase:false}) for profile hunt and qa, with a fixture project containing reviews/audit-x, .ultrapowers and .agents/ultrapowers.json.
On the host, run a harmless read-only form through the real hook: git --attr-source status version, then git --attr-source status -c alias.zz=version zz.
Do not run write or exec payloads on the host.
execution.observed_result: analyze() returned '' (allow) for all four payloads under hunt and qa, and denied `git -c alias.zz='!id' zz` and `git --attr-source HEAD status`. On the host, the real hook allowed both harmless forms and git printed its version, which shows the value consumed, `status` taken as the tree-ish, and the alias expanded. The write and exec payloads were not run on the host; their effect follows from git's documented behaviour, not from a run.

remediation.strategy: Fail closed on global options. Add --attr-source (and any other value-taking global option) to GIT_GLOBAL_WITH_ARG and handle its space form. Better, allow only a known set of no-value global options (--no-pager, -p, --paginate, --no-optional-locks, --bare, --literal-pathspecs, etc.). Deny any other dash-word before the subcommand, so no unknown global option can shift the subcommand. Add regression cases for `git --attr-source status commit`, `git --attr-source status -c alias.x=!id x` and `git --attr-source=HEAD status` in tests/qa-gatekeeper and tests/vulnerability-hunt.

likelihood.reason: Needs the agent to send the exact form, which prompt-injected content can do. Needs a git with --attr-source (2.40 or later, current in 2026).

impact.reason: It defeats the hunt's no-write, no-egress and no-project-code rules, and the QA and autopilot git rules. It also allows arbitrary host command execution through a git alias.

confidence.reason: Observed in the analyser inside the sandbox, and the key git behaviour (value consumed, -c processed) observed on the host through the real hook. The write and exec payloads were not run on the host.
